problem.name: SIGNED_SUBSUMPTION_TRANSPORT_DISCOVERY
problem.input: Two CNFs A and B over the same variable set V, here restricted to monotone width-2 formulas.
problem.question: Does there exist a signed permutation pi of V, extended by pi(-l)=-pi(l), such that for every clause C in A there exists D in B with D subseteq pi(C)?
problem.verification: Given pi and one witnessing B-clause for each A-clause, verification is polynomial.

theorem.claim: SIGNED_SUBSUMPTION_TRANSPORT_DISCOVERY is NP-complete, already on monotone 2CNF pairs that arise as the two siblings of one 3CNF parent.
construction: Let G=(V,E) be a simple graph on V={1,...,n}, n>=3.
Let A be the monotone 2CNF whose clauses are (x_i OR x_{i+1}) for the edges of the fixed cycle C_n, with indices modulo n.
Let B_G be the monotone 2CNF whose clauses are (x_u OR x_v) for every edge {u,v} in E(G).
Both A and B_G use the same n variables and contain no unit clauses.
forward_direction: If G has a Hamiltonian cycle, choose the variable permutation mapping the fixed cycle C_n to that Hamiltonian cycle and use no sign flips.
Every A-clause then maps exactly to a B_G-clause, hence the transport certificate exists.
reverse_direction: Suppose a signed permutation pi is a valid transport certificate.
Every pi(C) has width 2 and every B_G clause has width 2, so D subseteq pi(C) forces D=pi(C).
B_G is monotone. Since every variable occurs in the cycle A, any negative image pi(x_i) would occur in some pi(C) and could not equal a monotone B_G clause. Therefore all signs are positive.
Thus pi is an ordinary vertex permutation whose image sends every edge of C_n to an edge of G.
The image pi(C_n) is therefore a Hamiltonian cycle of G.
theorem.membership_in_NP: A signed permutation and clause witnesses form a polynomial-size certificate checkable in polynomial time.

sibling_lift.parent_3cnf: P_G = { z OR C : C in A } union { NOT z OR D : D in B_G }.
sibling_lift.effect: The NP-hardness therefore already holds when the two transport inputs are genuine siblings of one width-3 CNF parent.

effect_on_R44BP.meaning: R44BP is a genuine constructive safe-deletion primitive when a certificate is supplied, but generic discovery of that certificate class cannot be the missing polynomial L3 mechanism unless P=NP.
effect_on_R44BP.remaining_escape: The reduction does not force the parent to be maximum-deficiency-critical. A polynomial discovery theorem exploiting maxdef-critical sibling structure remains logically open.

next_exact_question: Does maximum-deficiency criticality force enough structure to make a nontrivial safe-deletion certificate polynomially discoverable on every critical sibling pair, or can an exact critical-family counterexample/barrier refute one fixed discovery rule?
